- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% of recent range.
- After sharp price spikes, model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 5–10% in next 3–5 days if sentiment remains neutral or slightly negative.
- If sentiment turns positive after a downtrend, model underreacts; increase forecast by 2–5% in next 3–7 days if sentiment is rising.
- Model overestimates mean reversion in short-term (1–3 days) after volatility spikes; apply a 3–5% downward bias if sentiment is weak or neutral.
- When sentiment is mixed or volatile, model tends to lag; add 1–3 days of lagged sentiment to forecast adjustment (e.g., if sentiment was negative 2 days ago, reduce forecast by 1–2%).
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates upward bias in bullish sentiment; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent 14-day average if sentiment > 0.10.
- If sentiment is consistently negative and price is trending down, model often fails to recognize support; add 2–5% buffer to forecast to avoid undershoot.
